minutes.headline: Sewer Commission held first hearings on irrigation meter, connection charge and grease trap rule changes; no vote until Nov 27.
minutes.summary: The Commission held the first of two public hearings on sewer regulation changes (single meter policy, irrigation meter policy, inflow/infiltration connection wording, grease trap rules). The second hearing is set for November 27 and no vote on the changes will occur until then. In the regular meeting it discussed a special town meeting transfer to the reserve capacity fund, the I&I evaluation RFP and a maintenance plan request, agreed drafts may be posted on the website, assessed a privilege fee at 654 Mass Ave and approved prior minutes.

budget_items.what_was_said: A fee is proposed for return visits when a meter is not working, plus an annual fee per meter, both deducted from irrigation credits.
Costs of reading and billing irrigation meters are currently spread over all users; the change would put them on program participants.
Connection charge wording clarified for the I&I sewer bank, with a capacity fee for large new flows.
Annual fees set for compliant and non-compliant establishments with internal and external traps; the commission may drop the percentage wording.
A special town meeting article would transfer reserve capacity fees to the stabilization fund to cover possible Fitchburg or Leominster charges.
Assessment for three new condo units after earlier assessment for the prior units.

what_happened.line: The Sewer Commission held the first of two public hearings on sewer regulation changes and set the second for November 27, with no vote until after it.
The proposed changes would move irrigation meter reading and billing costs from all sewer users to the participants in the irrigation program.
A special town meeting article would move reserve capacity fees into a stabilization fund against possible charges from Fitchburg or Leominster.
A motion to assess a privilege fee at 654 Mass Ave for three new condo units was made and seconded; the minutes do not record the outcome.
Draft documents may be posted on the website ahead of meetings, on counsel's advice, as a consensus practice rather than a vote.

why_it_matters: Sewer users who do not take part in the irrigation program could stop sharing the cost of reading and billing irrigation meters, while participants would pay fees through their irrigation credits.
Property owners adding units or large new flows may face a privilege fee or a capacity fee, and the 654 Mass Ave assessment is not confirmed in the minutes.
watch_next: Second public hearing on the sewer regulation changes on November 27, before any vote on them.
The I&I evaluation RFP scope and the maintenance plan draft, both expected on upcoming agendas.
